baseBranch: legion/LEGION-462-issue-pod (sjawhar/legion#1752, head 7e054d2ef1c4 at planning time); the implementer's first commit forward-merges it into legion/LEGION-631 and the pull request is based on it until #1752 merges
concerns: #1752 keeps moving under this branch: every forward merge re-runs the sandbox golden regeneration and TestEveryRolesPrivateVolumesMountInItsContainerAlone; a #1752 shape that blocks a step is reported on both issues before any workaround

Secret-update propagation into a running gVisor pod is unmeasured (the design rests on the kubelet's in-place refresh; this planner measured the 9p mount is cache=remote_revalidating and runsc's default --file-access-mounts is shared); task 0b measures it, fallback (daemon pushes hosts.yml over the launcher stream) needs the architect
Acceptance 1's literal `gh api user` is unmeetable for an App installation token (403 measured); the plan proves identity with gh api graphql viewer
The daemon and the worker image roll together (contract 16); a stale tree volume's /legion/worker-bin/gh is inert once nothing names it
On tmux the daemon's PATH must head with the real gh and a >=0.38 jj (the devbox's dotfiles gh wrapper acts as another App); the stage-3 scripts set that PATH where they start the daemon
Both former refusals (never merge, never write GitHub issues) become prose only; nothing enforces them
designSummary: Each role's App token is gh's own hosts.yml (plus a static config.yml with version "1") in a read-only directory GH_CONFIG_DIR names: in #1752's issue pod, two keys (github-hosts, github-config) of the role's existing private Secret <sandbox>-<role>-boot, projected as a fourth per-role volume gh-<role> at /var/run/legion/gh into that role's container alone; on tmux a per-claim 0700 directory of 0600 files under the state directory. git reads it through credential.helper=!gh auth git-credential. Each runtime refreshes its files from one daemon-provided GitHubCredential(ctx, role) function (appauth refreshWindow 5->20 min), Get/compare/Update per role Secret of each running pod. The gh shim, worker-bin, legion gh (both refusals), legion credential, /legion/v1/gh-token, /legion/v1/git-credential, /legion/v1/provisioning-credential, GrantRequest.push/pushTTL and the three tool-path pins go; the extension mints a grant only before a bash command that invokes legion (threads resolve, status). DaemonAPIVersion 15->16. Identity checks use gh api graphql viewer (REST /user answers 403 to an installation token).

findings.answer: Section 'The daemon API contract' and tasks 5-6: 15 (at #1752) -> 16 with its own paragraph, pi-legion package.json legion.daemonApiVersion, contracts fixture version.json; the boot gate and legion probe-image refuse a mixed pair.
findings.finding: The plan changed every surface the daemon API contract covers (credential routes, pane and pod environment) without bumping DaemonAPIVersion (api/version.go:3-17 bump rule).

findings.answer: Measured in the planner's gVisor pod that the Secret volume is a 9p mount with cache=remote_revalidating and the kubelet's ..data layout is visible; runsc's --file-access-mounts default is shared; stage 4b's token-rotation already reads a kubelet-renewed projected token in a gVisor pod. Task 0b measures a real Secret Update's propagation before any Go work, names the fallback (daemon pushes hosts.yml over the launcher stream) and stops for the architect if the file never refreshes.
findings.finding: Kubelet in-place Secret refresh under gVisor and the 1-minute propagation were asserted without measurement; the whole refresh design rests on them.

findings.answer: Task 11 rewrites it: CRED-GH = mise's gh, CRED-VIEWER/CRED-PR through plain gh, the gh pr merge line deleted (a real merge attempt is not a measured-safe proof); README.md:20 and :322-329 updated in task 10.
findings.finding: Stage 3's in-agent-credentials checkpoint (stage3-devbox-workflow.sh:1072-1083) asserts the worker-bin gh, two legion gh calls and the merge refusal, and would attempt a real gh pr merge once the refusal is gone.

findings.answer: Every write of the file logs 'github credential written'/'refreshed' with sandbox or claim, role, App and expiresAt; acceptance 3 runs right after token-rotation (architect container alive >= 48 min, pod kept), asserts the pod UID is unchanged, reads before's expiry from the log and waits until expiry + 60 s (<= ~12 min) for the 401.
findings.finding: The hour-boundary proof had no readable clock (nothing logs a lease's expiry) and no guarantee the pod lived across the window.

findings.answer: Section 'Existing shared clones on the tmux runtime': provisioning runs only when a claim is created or a retired claim restarts (outbox.go:466-469,500-505), so the daemon's boot runs configureRepositoryCredential with the new value on the project's clone; check named; pods re-provision at every launch.
findings.finding: Existing tmux shared clones keep credential.helper = !<state>/bin/legion credential; the plan did not say what rewrites them.

findings.answer: Section 'The credential file': every process that can run git in the shared clone is named with what it carries; daemon-side provisioning git uses the one-shot GIT_CONFIG override (clone.go:76-88) and never reaches the persisted helper; the tmux PATH precondition is stated and documented.
findings.finding: The PATH-resolved helper !gh auth git-credential could let a daemon-side git answer with the operator's own gh.

findings.answer: Measured: git credential approve/reject through the helper and gh auth git-credential store/erase exit 0 and leave the directory byte-identical (sha256 before and after).
findings.finding: gh auth git-credential was measured for get only; store/erase against a read-only GH_CONFIG_DIR were not.

findings.answer: Stated as new on both runtimes, added to both runtimeOwned sets, the <root>/gh creation (workspace_init.go:233) removed, docs/kubernetes.md's stale rows reconciled in task 10.
findings.finding: GH_CONFIG_DIR and the emptied GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_HOST were treated as already on panes/pods; they are new, runtime-owned, and the old <root>/gh directory and a stale docs row needed a decision.

findings.answer: Section 'The trust model, restated': the boundary now keeps identity (a review-role container never holds the implement token), not a write token off the volume; the provisioning-token tests stay with comments saying what they protect.
findings.finding: The trust-model sentence 'the init-container boundary still keeps the provisioning token off the tree volume' is false for implement-role containers, which now hold the same App's token.

findings.answer: Rewritten for #1752's one pod: exec into the implementer and reviewer containers of the same pod, each reads its own token and App, each mounts only gh-<its role>, shareProcessNamespace unset; TestEveryRolesPrivateVolumesMountInItsContainerAlone grows the volume; tmux has no cross-pane isolation by construction, which the spec accepts.
findings.finding: Acceptance 2 compared two pods' tokens and did not cover the one-pod case or tmux.

findings.answer: Section 'What is deleted': mint when splitShellCommands returns undefined (the safe default for a credential), the match is a legion word anywhere, a subagent stays exempt as today.
findings.finding: Narrowing needsGrant left the undefined-tokenisation case and the subagent exemption unstated.

findings.answer: LEGION_IMPLEMENT_APP_LOGIN/LEGION_REVIEW_APP_LOGIN on every tree launch (mintAtBoot returns both logins); missing or blank -> no bot-thread rule, not a failure (the daemon's nil-logins behaviour); added to the contract paragraph, docs table and the controller's tree-only list.
findings.finding: legion threads resolve's non-reviewer branch needs both App logins without the route; absence behaviour and the variable names were unregistered.

findings.answer: Each named in its task (tasks 4, 5, 7, 9, 10); FreePath goes with its callers using the plain PATH.
findings.finding: Six call sites of deleted or reshaped things were unnamed (workerbin.FreePath's two callers, workerbin.Path in tmux/environment.go, the grant rig's setup.sh/rig-mode.json/run.test.ts, the rig README rows, workspace_init.go:233, AGENTS.md rows and docs/kubernetes.md:1176).

findings.answer: Clause dropped; the check reads command -v gh, PATH without worker-bin (pod_env) and PI_SHELL_PREFIX; a stale shim is inert once nothing names it.
findings.finding: Acceptance 1's `test ! -e /legion/worker-bin` tests a persistent tree volume, not the branch.

findings.answer: Tied to task 0b's measurement; the prose at appauth.go:153-154 changes in task 2; consequences named (a mint every ~40 min per App, workspace-fetch's clone starts with >= 20 min of life).
findings.finding: refreshWindow 5->20 applies to every lease consumer and the constant's prose comment states the old figure.

findings.answer: Section 'What a worker loses and gains': both are prose in the merger prompt, the worker skill, merge-gate.md and the root AGENTS.md; nothing enforces them, deliberately, and the reviewer should not look for enforcement.
findings.finding: Where the never-merge and never-write-GitHub-issues rules live after the refusals go, and whether anything checks them, was unstated.

findings.answer: Section 'What is deleted': the pane's jj is PATH's and not held to minimumJJ (a pod's is the image's 0.45); a missing jj fails naming jj and PATH; on tmux the daemon's PATH heads with the jj it version-checked.
findings.finding: Dropping LEGION_JJ_PATH puts legion push/handoff complete on an unvalidated PATH jj with no stated refusal text.

implement: legion-worker — the push procedure, PR body, the implementer's own proof on the stage surfaces; references/cleanup-deletion.md for the deletion chain (CLI rows, docs, e2e), references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md for the forward merges of #1752, references/pr-body.md for the proof lines

specDepartures.evidence: Measured from this planner's pod with its own App token: `legion gh -- api user` answers HTTP 403 `Resource not accessible by integration` (GitHub refuses GET /user to an installation token); `gh api graphql -f query='{viewer{login}}'` answers `legion-reviewer[bot]`. packages/daemon/internal/api/real_github_test.go:62-74 already proves App identity with the same GraphQL query.

acceptance: 1. An implementer and a subagent it launches each run `gh api graphql -f query='{viewer{login}}'` (GitHub refuses `GET /user` to an App installation token) and push a commit with plain `gh` and `git`, with no grant minted and no `legion gh` on the path; the push is attributed to the implement App. A reviewer session pushes its handoff as the review App.

specDepartures.plan: The identity proof is `gh api graphql -f query='{viewer{login}}'` (answers the App's bot login) instead of `gh api user`; the push and everything else in the line stand.
specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 1: 'An implementer and a subagent it launches each run `gh api user` and push a commit with plain `gh` and `git`'.

workflowRecommendation: One implementer, tasks in the plan's order: 0a (merge #1752's head, base the PR on its branch) and 0b (measure Secret propagation under gVisor; stop and report if the mounted file never refreshes) before any Go work; whole-suite runs once at the end; stage 3 (devbox tmux) and stage 4b (this branch's image) are the live proofs, plus LEGION_REAL_GITHUB=1 TestRealGitHubCredentialSurface.
